caption:
Anthropic says Claude designed 318,484 proteins in 64 hours to grab onto five scorpion toxins.
Labs tested 211 of them, and 17 passed the binding test.
It is not an antivenom yet: nothing was tested in cells or animals.

Would you trust AI to help design the next antivenom?

slides.headline: Claude spent 64 hours designing *scorpion venom blockers*. 17 just passed real lab tests

slides.heading: *318,484* designs in 64 hours
paras: Anthropic asked Claude to design proteins that grab five scorpion neurotoxins, covering the part of each toxin that latches onto cells.
From one prompt and four follow-ups, it generated 318,484 designs in 64 hours.

slides.heading: *17 of 211* passed
paras: Claude picked 180 designs, researchers added 31, and Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience tested all 211 in the lab.
17 met the binding bar. The best two gripped Cn2, a toxin from a Mexican scorpion.

slides.heading: *1.2 million* stings a year
paras: Scorpions sting about 1.2 million people every year, and antivenoms are often costly or in short supply.
Anthropic is releasing all 211 designs and the lab data so other researchers can build on them.

slides.heading: Not an *antivenom* yet
paras: Anthropic calls this exploratory work. The proteins were only tested for binding, not in cells, animals or people.

paras.t: Whether they can stop venom is still unproven.

slides.hook: AI just took its first step toward cheaper antivenoms. Follow to see if these proteins survive the next tests.
